newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon readies first 10-year Eurobond. [CORRECTED 15:25 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Lebanon readies first 10-year Eurobond. [CORRECTED 15:25 GMT]

text.p: Lebanon is preparing to issue a 10-year $100 million Eurobond to finance improvements to its electricity network, central bank deputy governor Nasser Saidi said on Friday.
The issue is guaranteed by the World Bank and will have a spread of 100 basis points over equivalent U.S. Treasuries, Saidi told Reuters in a telephone interview.
It will be a bullet bond with repayment of capital in a lump sum at the end of the period, Saidi said (corrects by deleting reference to repayment of interest at end of period).

The overall structure of the bond had already been agreed, with Merrill Lynch International as lead manager, and it was now up to the Lebanese government to decide when to come to the market, Saidi added.

The beneficiary of the funds will be the state utility Electricite du Liban. They will finance part of a current $486 million programme for restructuring, expanding and modernising EDL's power supply and transmission.

The issue will be Lebanon's third sovereign venture on the international debt market and the spread will be significantly below the previous issues, due to the World Bank guarantee and increased investor confidence in Lebanon, Saidi said.

Lebanon's first three-year, $400 million Eurobond in 1994 had a spread of 325 basis points over equivalent U.S. Treasuries. Its five-year, $300 million issue in 1995 had a 320 bp spread over U.S. Treasuries and a further $100 million tranche of the five-year bond last May had a 295 bp spread.
Saidi said innovative elements of the new issue were the lower spread, longer maturity and matching between the project and the funding.
"The most innovative and interesting thing is that we have now got matching between the source of funding and the maturity of the project," Saidi said.

"This issue comes with a World Bank guarantee which means we have been able to extend the maturity to 10 years. Investors are also now much more comfortable with the Republic of Lebanon and Lebanon risk, which means we have been able to bring down the interest cost.
"With the World Bank guarantee the margin of only 100 basis points over equivalent U.S. Treasures is excellent," Saidi added.
